summary: SSE streaming stalls mid-generation during priority escalation and route-swap to dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customer LexiconHealth reports server-sent events (SSE) chat streams silent-pausing mid-token when the platform performs a priority escalation and swaps the request routing to a dedicated GPU pool. Impact: Multiple in-flight streaming chats for a small percentage (~0.6%) of requests into LexiconHealth's tenant stall for 6-20s of silence followed by either resumed stream or silent close. Environment: prod, us-east-1, dedicated tenant, observed on redwood-chat-3.5-dedicated and open-llama-7b-v2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send long-form streaming chat with chunked SSE enabled and per-request priority flag set to high. 2) Trigger autoscale/priority escalation by issuing several concurrent high-priority requests from same tenant. 3) Observe stream silence between SSE chunks during routing transition. Expected behavior: Stream should continue with minimal interruption or graceful handoff. Actual behavior: Stream pauses mid-token for many seconds without TCP FIN or SSE keepalive events; sometimes client reports connection still open but no data. Preliminary hypothesis: During priority escalation the routing layer performs an in-flight route-swap to a dedicated serving pool. The swap path currently moves the connection state asynchronously; a gap occurs where the worker continues generation but the SSE proxy stops forwarding chunks due to connection pinning with the previous router. NGINX/edge keepalive/proxy connection reuse prevents immediate reconnection, producing silent periods instead of errors. Additional factors: KV-cache pinning and staged worker eviction observed on nodes with heavy batching.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Aisha Kumar: Customer reported ~4 distinct chats stalled yesterday during peak processing window. Provided request ids and sample traces.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Liam): Requested tcpdump, client logs, and full request IDs; asked if customer is behind a corporate proxy (they are not).
2026-03-12 13:40 - Customer (LexiconHealth): Shared three request IDs and client-side timing: heartbeat frames continue but no SSE lines arrive for ~8s. No reconnect triggered by client.

2026-03-13 02:12 - SRE (Priya): Correlated request IDs to router logs. Observed route-swap events and a sequence where router A forwards first chunks then hands off to router B with no explicit proxy-level flush. Noted NGINX keepalive reuse between A and B.

2026-03-14 07:30 - Eng (Marco): Recreated in staging with controlled route-swap; observed identical silent gap when route pinning is released mid-generation. Proposed mitigation: serialize route handoff or stream proxy flush on swap.

2026-03-14 12:10 - Support (Liam): Applied temporary mitigation for LexiconHealth by disabling priority-escalation path for their tenant and forcing in-place worker processing. Customer reports no further stalls in 3 hours of monitoring.
2026-03-14 14:05 - Customer (LexiconHealth): Acknowledged mitigation and requested ETA for permanent fix and rollback plan.
investigation_notes: logs: router-A 2026-03-12T14:18:12.412Z request=rid:abcd1234 chunk=12 -> forwarded; router-A recorded route-swap to router-B at 14:18:12.419Z
traces: distributed trace shows worker continued generating tokens (token 13..18) but SSE proxy at router-B did not forward until 14:18:20.592Z
tcp captures: no FIN/RST during gap; keepalive pings continued on TCP connection; kernel retransmits negligible. Indicates application-layer stall rather than TCP drop.
heap/kv-cache: small eviction noted on worker node 7 around same timeframe; likely unrelated but worth investigating interaction with pinned KV state during handoff.
nginx config: connection reuse enabled via upstream keepalive; swap created a mismatch in backend connection mapping causing buffered data to sit at old proxy writer thread.
load: incident clustered around autoscale events (scale-up to dedicated pool) between 14:15-14:25 UTC; similar minor regressions seen in Canary on 2026-03-09.
attempted fixes: forced proxy flush on swap in staging removed the silent gap but introduced 1-2s latency spike; need a smoother approach.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-14: disabled priority-escalation route for LexiconHealth tenant and adjusted router config to avoid asynchronous connection pin release during swap. Immediate customer impact mitigated; monitoring confirms zero stalls in 4h post-mitigation. Next steps: engineering to implement atomic handoff (server-side stream relay) or graceful stream-forwarding with explicit flush on swap. Scheduler team to review autoscale handoff ordering and ensure KV-cache pin/unpin ordering. Target permanent fix in serving-runtime v1.14.2 with canary rollout 2026-03-21.
